title:
Someone ran `git push --force`
on the `main` branch.
3 weeks of commits evaporated.
subtitle: The developer wanted to squash a typo in their README commit. Instead, they force-pushed their local branch that was 42 commits behind origin, rewriting company history in 0.8 seconds.
logs: > Slack channel #dev-general erupts in collective panic.
> Developer: 'Wait, why is everyone pinging me?'
> Developer: 'I just wanted to fix my spelling mistake'.
> searching team laptops for who has the latest `git reflog`...
> running `git reset --hard origin/main` on 14 local workstations...
> 3 weeks of sprint work vanishes into the git object graveyard.
> branch protection rules have now been enabled (3 weeks late).
footnote: Error code: `FORCE-PUSH-DISASTER-404` · Commits vaporized: 42 · Branch protection: 'Oops'
pathTemplate: The code for `{path}` was in the repository 10 minutes ago, before someone force-pushed over it.
